title: Inbound authentication: SPF/DKIM/DMARC/ARC verification
description: Inbound mail authentication pipeline applied to every accepted message before routing. First: evaluate the mail-auth crate (stalwartlabs/mail-auth on crates.io) — it implements SPF RFC 7208, DKIM RFC 6376 (RSA-SHA256 and Ed25519-SHA256), DMARC RFC 7489, and ARC RFC 8617 in one dependency. Adopt if actively maintained and RFC-compliant; otherwise implement each protocol separately. Pipeline order: (1) SPF — validate connecting IP against MAIL FROM domain's SPF TXT record; (2) DKIM — verify all DKIM-Signature headers, fetch public keys via DNS, check body hash and header hash; (3) ARC — validate ARC-Authentication-Results / ARC-Message-Signature / ARC-Seal chain for forwarded/list mail; (4) DMARC — check SPF+DKIM alignment against From: domain, apply policy (none/quarantine/reject) per DNS record. Stamp Authentication-Results header (RFC 7601) onto message. Policy config: per-domain override table (e.g. known-good mailing lists exempt from DMARC reject). ARC is critical for mailing list mail — a valid ARC chain must excuse DMARC failure for List-ID-bearing messages.
